question_text: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his parents for difficulty breathing. He was playing outside in the snow and had progressive onset of wheezing and gasping. His history is notable for eczema and nut allergies. The patient has respirations of 22/min and is leaning forward with his hands on his legs as he is seated on the table. Physical examination is notable for inspiratory and expiratory wheezes on exam. A nebulized medication is started and begins to relieve his breathing difficulties. Which of the following is increased in this patient as a result of this medication?
